reviews.text: If I could give it one less star, I would. I took my cat to what I thought was a life-threatening emergency. He hadn't been able to urinate for half an hour, so I rushed him to the K Emergency Veterinary Clinic. The vet who saw me was dismissive and jumped to conclusions about my cat's diet, saying, "It's common; it's probably because of the Purina or other low-quality kibble you're giving him," knowing full well that he doesn't eat supermarket kibble. He told me, in a very curt manner, that urinary problems are the leading cause of death in male cats. His words were so guilt-inducing that I started to cry. He explained the medical procedures he wanted to perform—X-rays, catheterization, etc.—that he would keep him hospitalized for 48 hours, and told me to speak with his assistant about the cost. After a short wait, she handed me the bill without any explanation and left: €1144. I was ready to pay everything, but my friends and family warned me about the rather high price. When I asked to reduce the hospitalization to 24 hours so I could take my cat to my vet the next day to lower the bill, the vet tried to dissuade me and justified his prices by saying it was an emergency and a 24/7 facility. He explained that if I took him out, it wouldn't be much cheaper elsewhere and would only save me a maximum of €350. In the end, the bill was reduced to €502 for 24 hours. The next day, I came to pick up my cat and was again met with hostility. I had called ahead so they could prepare him, and the two assistants there asked me if I was there to collect a dead cat. I was a little flustered, and then after a few minutes they realized their mistake… Once at my vet's, he reassured me that urinary problems are indeed serious, provided they've been going on for 2-3 days and the cat is lethargic, depressed, and vomiting. Before that, it's perfectly fine to wait to see your regular vet instead of rushing to the emergency clinic. He also reassured me that his diet isn't necessarily the cause; even with special kidney food, cats can still have problems. It also depends on the individual cat. Finally, the next 24 hours at my vet's cost me €184. He focused on the essentials; the blood test was fine, so there was no need for X-rays, for example. I'm telling you my whole story to denounce the breach of trust and exploitation of distress at this emergency veterinary clinic, not to mention the exorbitant prices for a medical procedure that seems quite routine for a male cat. Charging upfront for unnecessary procedures is tantamount to theft. This is the first and last time I will ever go there, and I hope my experience will help future owners avoid being ripped off.

I'm giving one star somewhat reluctantly because the staff is genuinely caring; I was planning to take my kitten to this clinic, but after my encounter with the vet last night (who's probably the owner), I'm going to go elsewhere.

I brought my kitten, who's about six weeks old, because he had vomited and was weak. Without warning, he gave him two injections; not ideal, but I trust him and figure he knows what he's doing. Being naturally stressed and worried about Ebi, I started to cry. The vet told me I should be thinking about wars and children around the world (????). To which I replied that that makes me cry too (I'm not particularly bothered by the inappropriateness of his comments because, for me, the most important thing is that my kitten gets better and I don't like to cause a scene, but it was still quite inappropriate to say that kind of thing to someone who was already anxious).

The veterinary assistant who was present was more empathetic and reassuring, and I thank her for that.

About an hour and a half after my visit, my kitten's condition worsened. He stood up suddenly and then fell, unable to open his eyes, whereas before the visit he had just been a little lethargic but was meowing and able to move around.
I called them to find out what substances had been injected, and I heard the veterinarian talking about me, calling me a hypochondriac in a rather haughty and disdainful manner.
The woman I spoke to on the phone, who wasn't there when I was seen, was lovely and tried to reassure me as best she could, even though I still don't understand why they injected morphine into a kitten who had "only" vomited his milk (which I had bought at the same clinic earlier that day) and who, according to the veterinarian, was perfectly fine. This man is truly lucky to have such a good team, but it won't be enough for me to entrust my two animals to them for treatment, nor will it be enough to recommend them to anyone I know.

If you still want to try it, here's a tip: make sure the owner isn't there when you go.

I brought my dwarf rabbit in as an emergency; he was infested with fleas, and the only solution the vet could offer was euthanasia.

Despite informing him that I had a cat and a two-and-a-half-year-old child at home, he gave me no advice or recommended any products to eradicate the fleas.

The result: an infested apartment a few days later, another infected pet, and my son and I covered in bites.
I had to seek a second opinion from a vet and a pharmacist to get any help.
I absolutely do not recommend this clinic, especially since the cost for the consultation, euthanasia, and cremation was nearly €600! They could at least have taken preventative measures and avoided a health risk that could have been serious for all of us!

In my case, I brought in my dog ​​who was very unwell; it turned out she had a very large tumor. I had to say goodbye to her, and I am very grateful to Dr. Handi Dahmana, who was particularly kind and considerate. He took the time to thoroughly explain the process, the possibilities, and the drawbacks. Of course, treating an animal is expensive, and when you take in an animal, you have to be able to care for it, save it, or say goodbye, regardless of the cost.

Thank you again for everything.

Many additional tests were performed on my cat (for the small sum of 1000 euros!), yet no diagnosis was made. In fact, the abscess he had was visible during the clinical examination and was very accurately diagnosed at a normal price in another clinic. It's fortunate that these people "only" "deal with animals"...
Very warm welcome

"Emergency" – don't take it seriously. I went there Saturday night at 11 PM with my dog, who hadn't eaten or drunk anything since morning. The receptionist told me to come in so they could examine him. When I arrived, I waited a good 20 minutes, hearing snickering from another room… No one came. That's when the receptionist told me the vet recommended I go to the hospital for a tonsil ultrasound. This vet, whom we've never seen, and she hasn't even seen the dog. I then asked him if it would be possible to at least give him a visual examination, instead of just relying on the symptoms and prescribing an anti-inflammatory, given that his lips were swollen. He replied that the vet had finished her shift and he didn't know when the next on-call vet would arrive. So I told him it was absurd to give a diagnosis without examining the animal. He replied that the vet had years of study and therefore knew what she was talking about. Frankly, I'm dealing with two people who have no business being in an emergency veterinary clinic.

I don't know what kind of response my comment will get. But know that you haven't chosen the right profession.

I'm sorry for the other veterinarians practicing here, and I doubt they're all as heartless as these two, but on August 15th at 11 PM, the vet on duty should consider changing careers.
According to the opinion of the emergency clinic at 3 Luc, which is much more reputable, letting an animal leave without giving it a sedative is not normal.
Thank you, Dr. Armand! For your patience despite not knowing the language and for taking such good care of my pet. Thank you so much!
A very good experience; we were on vacation and, since we didn't speak the language, they were very patient with us and treated our dog wonderfully. Very good treatment
Thank you for what you do for animals in distress who have no one to help them; you deserve the Legion of Honour.
A very good veterinarian who takes care of abandoned cats who have no one to care for them. Thank you, Doctor.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

If I could give zero stars, I would.

I went to this so-called emergency vet on a Sunday for my Staffordshire Bull Terrier, who had been bitten on the neck by another dog. The receptionist told me it wouldn't necessarily cost more than €200; he was understanding and very professional. Thank you to him.

However, the vet clearly doesn't like his job. He handled the dog carelessly, telling me directly, without even touching the dog, just by looking at the wound, that he was going to operate immediately and that my dog ​​would need to be operated on under general anesthesia, which was completely unnecessary!

So I went back to reception to arrange payment in installments since €400 wasn't an option for me, and that's when the vet spoke very rudely to the receptionist. So I left and I was very, very glad I did because I changed vets, I went to another vet who took very good care of my dog, treating the wound without anesthesia and without stitches, with a prescription and disinfectant, all for €150.

I strongly advise against this veterinary clinic.

My cat was found by animal control after being hit by a car. They took her to this clinic where we were told they had done all the necessary x-rays and tests and that, in the end, she wasn't seriously injured. They even told us we could take her home.

In the end, we paid almost €600 in one day for the tests, medication, and everything else.

Once we got home, we could clearly see that she wasn't well. She was breathing through her mouth, had trouble swallowing, and was clearly in pain. Despite this, they let us leave with large pills to give her, even though her mouth and throat were swollen.

So we decided to see another veterinarian, and thank goodness we did. He was shocked. He examined her throat and discovered that she did indeed have something stuck there, her nose was completely blocked, and she had a hematoma in her mouth and another on her ear. That's why she was breathing through her mouth. He also told us that the pills weren't at all suitable for her condition and that she should have been given a liquid treatment with a dropper. He gave her two injections to relieve her pain before starting a more appropriate treatment.

The most shocking thing is that the first clinic told us she had probably just fallen, while the second vet confirmed that she had indeed been run over.

Honestly, I'm disgusted. I feel like they didn't take my cat's condition seriously. Looking at reviews afterward, I saw that many other people had had bad experiences, and unfortunately, I understand why. If I had seen this before, I never would have gone. Unfortunately, we didn't choose this clinic; the animal shelter took our cat there.

I'm sharing my experience to prevent others from going through the same thing.

Avoid at all costs!!!
THEY ALMOST KILLED MY CAT!!! AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!! + huge lack of respect from the staff (proof available if needed), for the sake of your animals, NEVER put them in this "clinic"

A huge THANK YOU 🙏 to Dr. Handi Dahmana and the entire team at the K Emergency Veterinary Clinic. Thanks to their responsiveness, professionalism, and kindness, my little Grisette, 16 years old, was able to have surgery in time and avoid the worst!

Dr. Dahmana took the time to explain everything, reassure me, and find the best solution to treat Grisette. We also received a warm welcome from the whole team, which immediately put us at ease.

I want to emphasize that you do remarkable work, both for our companion animals and for abandoned or abused animals. Your dedication deserves to be recognized. 😇

A thousand thanks from me 🙏… and especially from Grisette 😻.
They had my little cat in emergency hospitalization a while ago, they were great and didn't give up until they found the problem.

My mother and I came in as an emergency because our little Pomeranian had an eye ulcer. We waited almost an hour, even though we were alone in the waiting room; I understand there are emergencies, no problem. But is that a reason to speak to us like dirt once we were in the consultation room? To dare tell us that if we didn't muzzle him, you weren't even taking care of him while he was suffering?! Our 11-month-old Pomeranian is fearful and therefore aggressive; instead of reassuring him, he muzzled him with a rope, incredibly tightly, anyway... When my mother explained what happened, he had the nerve to tell her to cut it short, dismissing her, and then he made her feel guilty???? It's a collective hallucination at this point! Since then, our little Pomeranian is terrified of eye drops and ointment; Before this ordeal, we could give him saline solution without any problem, but now we can't even approach him without him becoming aggressive. So yes, you treated our dog, but with utterly appalling methods. If you don't like animals, Dr. Armand Kniasian, you should consider a different profession!
Excellent service, my dog ​​Luna was very well cared for, and I especially thank Dr. Armand. I highly recommend this very professional veterinary clinic.

At the end of June, I brought my cat in for emergency treatment due to breathing difficulties. After sedation for blood work and examinations, the vet diagnosed a very high fever and severe dehydration.

They suggested hospitalization with IV fluids. I asked if we could take him home so his regular vet could administer the IV fluids the next day.

They gave him an injection to bring him out of the sedation.

He died 15 minutes after leaving the clinic.

Given his condition and the obvious dehydration, the vet should have suggested rehydrating him even before performing the tests.

When I asked if we could take him home, I should have clearly stated that he was at risk of dying, which was never mentioned.

According to his regular vet, the two injections worsened his condition, but this cannot be definitively confirmed.

First appointment following an emergency because my dog ​​had eaten a cactus (yes, apparently it happens, haha).
Excellent care, lovely team. Everything was sorted out. I made an appointment to have my dog ​​operated on, as he only has one testicle. The vet I saw that day told me he could handle it without any problems. The day of the appointment arrived, my dog ​​had been fasting since the previous evening, and I was informed that he wouldn't be operated on. Another vet explained that the operation was risky, especially since they didn't know where the other testicle was, and there was a possibility that he only had one, meaning it would be pointless to operate. Luckily, this doctor took the time to explain everything to me thoroughly; otherwise, my young dog would have been operated on unnecessarily. So, I have mixed feelings… thank you again to this man who gave me detailed information and prioritized my dog's well-being.
Thank you for your comment!

I came in as an emergency because my dog ​​had a prickly pear cactus in his ear. The vet took care of him immediately and was able to remove it without anesthesia. Perfect! We even received some helpful advice on ear care.
Thank you for your comment!

Hello,

Thank you for taking the time to leave us a review, although we regret that your experience at our clinic was not entirely satisfactory.

As we did not receive a comment accompanying your 2-star rating, we unfortunately do not know what led to your disappointment. If you would be willing to share your feedback with us, we would be happy to listen and understand what did not meet your expectations and, where possible, improve our services.

Sincerely,
The K Emergency Veterinary Clinic Team

I was seen quickly for a digestive problem. Veterinarian Marinescu took the time to analyze the issue, answered all my questions, and gave me a treatment that was effective that same evening. Thank you!
I've been bringing my dog ​​here since he was born, and we've always been very well received and his needs met.

We were seen very well and quickly at the clinic for our dog who had gotten a foxtail in his ear, even though we arrived at 7 pm as an emergency. The veterinarian was very kind, efficient, and helpful. The reception was also excellent; thank you to the whole team, I highly recommend the clinic!

He faked his Google rating. He almost killed my dog ​​nine years ago. I don't understand why he's still practicing. Where are his qualifications? Bought online like his reviews? My two-month-old puppy had been bitten and needed surgery. I got a call the next day telling me to come pick her up quickly because she had barked and cried all night. They bandaged her and applied honey, for a total of over 300 euros. According to them, there was nothing more they could do. On Monday, I took her to my regular vet. The wounds were infected, and she had to have two operations to survive. Her life was in danger. Since then, my dog ​​trembles every time I walk into a vet's office.

Mathieu

Avoid at all costs. I took my cat in as an emergency, they kept him for half a day, did some tests, and charged me nearly €500 without being able to detect anything serious.

A week later, my cat was still in the same condition. My usual vet immediately diagnosed cancer.

I mostly felt like I paid a huge bill for wasting time while my pet's condition worsened. No empathy, no real care, just a hefty bill. Shameful.

Response to your review:

My cat died.

Your response still doesn't answer my question: how could such a serious lung condition, with respiratory distress, not be clearly identified or suspected? Your response was, "Your cat has inflammation."

I felt the care was very standardized, with a lack of empathy in the face of a critical situation.

The feeling that the financial aspect took precedence during a time of great distress is very difficult to accept.

My cat was then taken care of elsewhere at a much lower cost with a real veterinarian.

Top-notch veterinary clinic! My dog ​​was attacked and had to have surgery at night. We picked her up the next morning, and they explained the necessary aftercare. The team is fantastic, from the vet to the reception staff; everyone is kind and caring. It's a shame they don't have a sixth star.

I arrived at the emergency vet clinic one evening, not knowing what was wrong with my cat, but she was in critical condition, which had developed in seconds.

She was immediately given pain medication, and I was told to go home and that they would keep me updated.
I didn't hear anything all night, so I called first thing in the morning and was told to come pick her up and take her to her regular vet.
I arrived right away, and they told me they had simply kept her on pain medication but suspected internal bleeding and didn't have a CT scan to confirm it.
She didn't survive and died about an hour after arriving at the regular vet's office, who confirmed the diagnosis. How can they claim to handle emergencies without the proper equipment? I wish they had told me right away, and I would have taken her to La Valentine... we certainly could have saved her, but the bill would have been for another vet center, so they kept her all night, letting her bleed out... Then, to top it all off, I called them to tell them she had died, and they replied, "Well, you should have felt it, she had a lump." Of course, I'm the vet!
If you have a pet in critical condition, don't go there; you might regret it for years to come.

A team of exceptional compassion.
Veterinary emergencies are always stressful, but the reception and the staff were incredibly kind and caring, both to my pet and to me.
You can tell they are truly passionate about their work. A huge thank you for your care and kindness.

Absolutely disappointed...
I recently took my 14-year-old cat in for a check-up because of some vomiting and a lump near her front paws. I had to leave her at the clinic and pick her up that same evening while they did the tests. The vet told me there would be a quote of €260 plus any treatment needed... But there's no paperwork to confirm this, no record of the quote. At the time, I wasn't too worried and just wanted my cat to be well taken care of. However, after the consultation and the results, which were explained to me hastily, the receptionist asked me to pay €409 for the additional tests, even though I hadn't been informed beforehand. Furthermore, the tests clearly showed higher than normal urea and tuberculin skin test results, but only an anti-nausea medication was prescribed... I'm going back to another vet with the results so I can get a real explanation and not leave my cat with a possible kidney problem... and as for the infamous "lump" that my boyfriend and I had noticed, the vet told me there was nothing wrong with it, but I'm convinced he didn't even look at it.

I understand that consultations cover a lot of things, which can explain the sometimes high prices, but here, €409 for an anti-nausea medication just to tell me my cat wasn't going to die from a kidney problem is a steep price to pay... they should find another profession, huh?

Avoid this clinic!

Dr. Armand Kniasian, the clinic's director, physically threatened me. I had to call the police.

Judging by other comments, this is unfortunately not an isolated incident. Several people report abusive behavior, both psychological and physical, towards clients who are already vulnerable and come seeking care for their pets.

I will explain in detail:

On May 30, 2026, I went to the clinic with my cat. He was showing several worrying symptoms: fever, loss of appetite, dehydration, and blood in his urine.

I explained to the staff that my cat had always been healthy, that he was up-to-date on his vaccinations and parasite treatments, and that I had recently moved into an apartment in Marseille. The apartment across from mine was unoccupied and infested with pigeons. My cat was scratching a lot, and I thought his symptoms might be related to that.

The clinic gave me a quote for numerous tests at a very high price. I indicated that I wanted, initially, a PCR test for diseases transmitted by pigeons, as well as treatment to reduce his fever while waiting for the results.

I paid 240 euros. After the consultation, no one told me which medication had been administered, and I wasn't given a receipt.

Seeing that his condition hadn't improved, I returned to the clinic the next day to request further treatment. Dr. Kniasian received me disrespectfully and refused to administer or prescribe any other treatment. I then stayed at the clinic to obtain the invoice for the services provided, an invoice that should have been given to me on the first day.

From that moment on, Dr. Kniasian's behavior seemed designed to emotionally destabilize me so that I would leave without receiving the bill. He also indicated that he might not send the PCR test to the lab, even though I had already paid for it the day before. I told him that I no longer trusted him and that I wanted a refund.

The situation then escalated. While I was calling the police, Dr. Kniasian physically threatened me and took my cell phone from my hands. When other clients entered the clinic, he called me "crazy" in front of them.

Faced with this, I decided to stay until the police arrived. Only then did the doctor calm down and stop his insults.

Two days later, lacking the funds after the expenses incurred at that clinic, my cat was taken to a social veterinary clinic. From the very first examination, the team identified a wound on the inside of his thigh that had progressed to a generalized infection. This diagnosis was made following a thorough and careful physical examination. Part of the wound was already necrotic.

What shocks me is that a great deal of time was spent convincing me to agree to a series of expensive tests, even though this wound, though clearly visible (see photo of the already treated wound), had gone undetected.

I felt that the focus was more on performing these tests than on immediately finding the visible cause of my cat's condition. Given the size of the wound, I find it hard to understand how it could have gone unnoticed.

Furthermore, a local woman I happened to meet while transporting my sick cat spontaneously shared her own reservations about his behavior and the cost of his consultations. This conversation reinforced my feeling that I wasn't alone in this situation.

I'll let everyone draw their own conclusions, but this experience was extremely distressing, especially since I was simply trying to get my sick cat treated.

Honestly, this clinic is one to avoid.

I just got off the phone with them and I felt like I was annoying the vet from the very beginning. Instead of listening carefully to what I was explaining about my cat's situation, he immediately became defensive.

His words were: "We're not responsible, and it's none of our business what happens outside our clinic or what happens to your cat."

Yet, I didn't accuse anyone. I simply explained what had happened at another veterinary clinic and stated that I wanted to go to a different one. Nothing more.

I mostly felt that he was more concerned about something else than my pet's health. Seeing people with so little empathy caring for our companions is truly frightening. Such an attitude inspires absolutely no confidence when it comes to entrusting someone with your pet's health.

Furthermore, I was quoted €91 for a consultation with no specific treatment whatsoever, when I initially only asked for information about sterilization. At that price, I'd rather spend my money elsewhere, especially given the attitude and lack of consideration I witnessed.

And before you reply to systematically defend your veterinarian, please know that I was present during this phone conversation. I know perfectly well what was said, but more importantly, how it was said to me. My review accurately reflects my experience.

It's a shame it's impossible to give zero stars, because that's exactly the rating this experience deserves.
Thank you for your kind comment, the K Emergency Team!

I do not recommend this clinic.

I went there as an emergency because my 10-month-old dog had a foxtail in her nose. Upon arrival, I was quoted €360 for the procedure.

After two anesthetic injections (and my dog ​​was still responsive during the examination), the veterinarian was unable to remove the foxtail. He told me it was already too far into her nasal passages (which was surprising given how quickly it had become lodged there, according to other medical opinions) and that an endoscopy at another clinic would be necessary.

So I left with a €150 bill for a procedure that didn't work, and my dog ​​who received two injections without any results.

At the second clinic, the veterinarian was able to remove the foxtail immediately, using the same technique, without needing an endoscopy. This procedure cost €260, which is €100 less than the quote from the first clinic.

I understand that these situations can be uncertain, but in this case, the diagnosis and information provided proved inaccurate. This experience wasted my time and money and made the procedure more difficult for my dog.

I will not return to this clinic, neither for emergencies nor for routine checkups.

❗️AVOID THIS VETERINARIAN❗️
After reading numerous comments similar to mine, I urge everyone to contact the veterinary board.

I took my 1-year-old dog to the emergency vet after she was violently hit by a scooter at 7 a.m. right in front of me. It was an extremely traumatic experience for both of us. The handling during the X-ray (which was quite rough) was questionable, but so far, nothing serious; I figured it was their job.

Then, the vet immediately started his sentence in a condescending tone, asking, "You give your dog bones?" to which I replied that I didn't. He then persisted, mentioning bones in her stool and accusing me of lying. I found this attitude particularly inappropriate and completely unprofessional. I was also accused of lying about my dog's bowel movements, claiming I hadn't defecated for two days (which is completely false!).

Please note, I'm not questioning the information revealed by the x-ray, but it would be good if they did their job and looked into the problems observed instead of accusing owners with lies.

Regarding the diagnosis, the explanations were very limited. Only one lateral x-ray was taken (SHAMEFUL for a dog that had just been hit by a car), the vet telling me he couldn't take a frontal x-ray because "my dog ​​won't let me put her on her back," in an accusatory tone. I should mention that she's a very sweet dog and not at all aggressive; she just doesn't like being forcibly pinned on her back, like 99% of dogs, really… Despite the lack of further examinations, he mentioned a pelvic fracture without really explaining what he was basing this conclusion on. I asked him questions, but he didn't answer; he simply pointed at the x-ray. His recommended course of action: rest for a month, no jumping, and if she wouldn't cooperate, a crate.

Afterward, when I spoke with the assistant, she explained that no fracture had been clearly visualized and that "he had concluded that."

In the end, €250 for a two-minute examination and a very vague diagnosis. So I sent the x-ray to several veterinarians I know, who confirmed that this diagnosis didn't really make sense. With just one X-ray like this, it's impossible to see the entire body or make a reliable diagnosis. At the very least, a frontal X-ray, as well as other tests (blood work, ultrasound, etc.) to examine the organs, would have been necessary, which wasn't done.

I won't go into all the details of what was explained to me afterward, but several points were never mentioned during the consultation, and I was also told that the so-called bones in her stool weren't necessarily in her stool, but since there were no other X-rays, nothing is certain…

It's appalling to allow such people to practice these days!

I received confirmation afterward, from a reliable source, that this clinic is known for being fraudulent and highly incompetent.

I think this person's pride blinds them to their scientific and human capabilities. Please do not reply to me, I am not interested in justifications to cover up this man's incompetence (nothing for the girls, they were lovely).

I want to thank the entire team at this veterinary clinic for their kindness, professionalism, and compassion throughout Boris's adoption process 🐾

From the very beginning, I received excellent support throughout the entire adoption process. The team always took the time to answer my questions with great patience.

The follow-up was also impeccable regarding booster vaccinations, advice given, and all the care surrounding neutering and microchipping.

Thank you again for your warm welcome, your patience, and the love you give to all your little residents ❤️
Smile, you're on camera!!! Very welcoming, we even saw the assistant eating her cucumber 🥒 A bit pricey, but the treatments are worth the cost. 😜🤪😝😛 …

Stay away from this place if you want your animal to live. We left there a pigeon that could not open her mouth (they said they can handle it) its been 36 hours and it was not treated at all. Evidently she will starve to death .who said vaeteriners loves animal. 😡 They loves money. …

I cannot thank this clinic enough for helping my dog, Coco. We came in with a very stressful situation, his ear was bleeding and he was in a lot of pain.
The receptionist was incredibly kind and understanding, he saw how much Coco was suffering and let us see the doctor right away, even though it wasn't our turn yet. The doctor was so professional and gentle. He found a long grass awn (épillet) deep in the ear that had caused a popped eardrum. He managed to remove it safely and explained everything so clearly.
It is such a relief to find a team that truly cares about animals and acts so quickly in an emergency. Highly recommend them to anyone in Marseille! Thank you again for saving our holiday and helping Coco feel better.
Top-notch vet, clear explanations!

I had to take my cat in several times over two weeks due to urinary problems. Enki received excellent care, as did I and my anxieties as a cat mom. The staff were attentive, took the time to explain everything, and I know that if I have any doubts, I can call them for advice. While the bills were still high, they kept costs down as much as possible and even offered some treatments. They were wonderful for both my cat and me. Thank you to the veterinarians who cared for Enki, and to all the assistants for their availability.

I went there a while ago and received a misdiagnosis that could have led to my dog's death if I hadn't rushed her to the Massilia clinic in the middle of the night. They treated her (pyometra). The vet at this emergency clinic thought it was just a simple inflammation and that my dog ​​was playing on my anxiety! I had already posted this review last year, but it was deleted! Avoid at all costs.

For a cat suffering from dental pain: Friendly welcome from the reception staff and very little wait for a Saturday. The vet was gentle with the frightened cat. Pain relieved, but a return visit is necessary for a dental cleaning.
A very professional and very humane veterinary clinic

A very bad experience. Around 8 pm, I called to say that my dog ​​had eaten grass during our walk, but there were foxtails in it. She started choking and trying to make herself vomit. So I called the clinic on the hamstring, explaining the situation. The veterinary assistant told me to come in immediately before 9 pm because there would be a change of vet. I arrived there, they checked me in, and the vet let us in. I explained that she must have eaten foxtails. My dog ​​kept clearing her throat and had trouble swallowing. Without even putting her on the examination table, my dog, on the floor, touched her throat and said, "She has tracheitis!" "Sir, I'm telling you she ate foxtails!" he exclaimed. And he replied, "You must have given her a cold bath or left the air conditioning on. A dog doesn't swallow foxtails!" I asked him to open her mouth so he could look, and I had to carry her onto the examination table myself. He still gave her an antibiotic injection for nothing, telling me she'd be fine in an hour! He charged me €232 for absolutely nothing, and said if she wasn't better, to come back tomorrow, that he'd sedate her and examine her, but it had to be done now, not tomorrow! The next day, I took my dog ​​to my vet, who examined her and ran the necessary tests. The foxtails had passed into her esophagus, and sure enough, that night she vomited up all the grass and no fewer than three foxtails!
